hypothesis: Same-source six-language preparation can share source analysis and background separation, but any visual repair defect propagates to every language. Source-local classical inpainting produced obvious patches; local LaMa improved text removal but left soft clothing/hair, apple/hand ghosting and source-colour/glyph fragments at transitions. These candidate videos remain revise. Exact native script, actual mixed-audio DTW, independent transcription, decoded glyph boundary measurements and mux timebase correlation are separate evidence. An invalid optional accent was rejected at createTask; singleton JSON review envelopes were recovered locally from saved receipts without another charge. One source and six locales are not six independent source validations.
limitations: Source-burned captions overlap moving clothing, hair, apple and fingers. Repairs create visible soft regions/ghost edges and occasional source-colour/glyph fragments around text transitions.
Uniform green native subtitles simplify the original per-word green/red/white highlight animation.
Native female dubbed audio retains original English mouth movements; no lip synchronization was performed.
Audio preservation is supported by local source separation, original post-7.8s samples, and external model perception; lossless separation is not claimed.
Same-Agent review plus external audio model and pixel/ASR measurements is not independent native-speaker, company or business acceptance.
Hindi exact-copy verification remains pending because the actual audio transcript uses alternate negation/nasal spellings.
promotion: Requires scoped evidence and developer/company review; not loaded by retrieval
